text:
emma: Hey team — running into a flaky cert verification error on Windows that only shows up in a venv with Python 3.12 + async client (httpx in our SDK).

raj: ugh, details? error message?

emma: error is `ssl.SSLCertVerificationError: [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed: unable to get local issuer certificate` when calling `client.chat.completions.create(...)` from an async script. Synchronous calls fine.

mike: is this on system python or python.org build?

emma: python.org 3.12.0 on Win11. Repro steps: create venv, pip install redwood-sdk, create async example using `async with AsyncClient(...)` and you get verify failure within first request.

sarah: can you paste minimal repro?

emma: sure — gist style: 
```python
import asyncio
from redwood import AsyncClient

async def main():
    async with AsyncClient(api_key=... ) as c:
        await c.chat.completions.create(model='rwd/mini', input='hi')

asyncio.run(main())
```
stack: `ssl.SSLCertVerificationError` from `ssl.create_default_context().load_verify_locations()`

raj: does `import certifi; print(certifi.where())` work in that venv?

emma: certifi is installed, points to /.../site-packages/certifi/cacert.pem. Forcing cafile to certifi fixes it (workaround):
```python
import ssl, certifi
ctx = ssl.create_default_context(cafile=certifi.where())
# pass ctx into httpx or aiohttp connector
```

mike: interesting that sync path didn't hit it — maybe our async transport uses a different SSLContext or uses schannel adapter on sync path. Which transport is the SDK using for async?

emma: httpx.AsyncClient (httpcore backend) per default. Sync uses requests on our older shim in this app.

sarah: might be a windows store cert lookup bug in httpcore + Python 3.12 openssl config. We saw similar edgecases but not this exact combination. Can you share pip freeze?

emma: pip freeze: httpx==0.24.0, httpcore==0.17.0, certifi==2024.6.0, redwood-sdk==0.10.4

raj: thanks. @mike can you try repro on a Win box? I can also try on WSL.

mike: spinning one up. Quick thought: venv activation on Windows can sometimes shadow system CA store access if PYTHONHTTPSVERIFY or SSL_CERT_FILE is set in env. Any env vars?

emma: nope, nothing set. Removing venv (use global python) makes calls succeed. So it seems venv isolation prevents default Windows cert store from being used by httpcore/openssl.

ci-bot: Note: test flake detected — tls-windows-async on windows-latest in CI failed 1/10. Ticket created #TICK-4721

raj: good catch CI. That lines up. Maybe our async transport doesn't call `SSLContext.set_default_verify_paths()` the same way. Workaround in SDK: if on Windows, prefer to build SSLContext pointing at certifi.where() when env SSL_CERT_FILE absent.

sarah: agree but we should be careful — some enterprise customers rely on machine-installed CAs (company root) in Windows store. Overriding with certifi would drop those.

emma: yeah, we only need to fallback when default lookup fails. Proposed change: on import, try `ssl.create_default_context()` + `ctx.get_ca_certs()` check. If empty on Windows venv, try certifi as fallback and warn.

mike: can we detect Win + venv easily? `sys.platform == 'win32' and hasattr(sys, 'real_prefix')` is brittle. Maybe just rely on a failing handshake detection to trigger fallback at runtime with a single retry.

raj: prefer a single retry at request time. Retry plan: if TLS verify fails, attempt one retry with context from certifi and log a visible warning suggesting user install certifi or configure SSL_CERT_FILE.

sarah: add a debug env var to force the fallback for local repro `REDWOOD_PY_SSL_FALLBACK=1`. Also log a short snippet for SRE.

emma: I can open a PR with a minimal retry wrapper around httpx AsyncClient send. Will include tests for Windows CI job and a short doc blurb for onboarding.

mike: pls include a changelog entry and mention the security considerations.

raj: thx. tagging @sre later to see if we want this in patch or minor release. Also add a one-off CI job to run Python 3.8/3.10/3.12 windows matrix for this test.

emma: will do. For now my local workaround is `export SSL_CERT_FILE=$(python -c \"import certifi; print(certifi.where())\")` (PowerShell tip: `$env:SSL_CERT_FILE=$(python -c \"import certifi; print(certifi.where())\")`).

sarah: thanks for the repro and workaround — big help.

emma: filing the PR in a few hours, will link the CI job and the ticket. :thumbsup:
